questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the split verdict of the Supreme Court in January 2026 on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988:
1. Justice B.V. Nagarathna held that the provision violates Article 14.
2. Justice K.V. Viswanathan struck down the provision, while Justice Nagarathna upheld it.
3. Because of the split, the matter goes to the Chief Justice of India for a larger bench.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Justice Nagarathna struck down Section 17A (prior approval before probing a public servant's official decisions), reasoning that it breaches Article 14 and that Section 19 already protects officials at the prosecution stage; Justice Viswanathan upheld it, but only if approval comes from an independent authority such as the Lokpal or Lokayuktas. Statement 2 swaps the two opinions. A two-judge split is sent to the CJI (Surya Kant) to constitute a larger bench.
questions.s: All India Radio News; Drishti IAS, 30 Jan 2026

questions.q: In January 2026 the Supreme Court held that Tiger Global's 2018 sale of its Flipkart stake to Walmart is taxable in India. Which one of the following best describes the Court's reasoning on treaty benefits?
o: Indirect transfers of Indian assets lie outside India's tax net once the seller holds a Tax Residency Certificate
A Tax Residency Certificate alone does not guarantee India-Mauritius DTAA benefits where the real 'head and brain' of the entities lay outside Mauritius
A Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement can never be examined for treaty shopping by Indian courts
The shares were held for over 24 months and were therefore exempt under the treaty
questions.e: The Court restored the 2020 Authority for Advance Rulings order and looked beyond the paperwork: a Tax Residency Certificate is evidence of residence but does not by itself entitle an entity to treaty relief if it is a conduit controlled from elsewhere. The other options state the opposite of this substance-over-form approach, and the tax demand was nearly Rs 14,500 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court has directed all States to frame a policy on police media briefings within three months, modelled on a manual prepared by an amicus curiae.
2. The Supreme Court agreed to examine petitions by Tamil Nadu and Kerala on whether the Enforcement Directorate is a juristic person entitled to approach High Courts under Article 226.
3. In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh (2026), the Court lowered the age of consent under the POCSO Act, 2012 to 16 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The briefing policy follows a manual by amicus Gopal Sankaranarayanan, and the States argue that a statutory body like the ED has only the powers expressly granted, so cannot sue under FEMA or PMLA. In Anurudh the Court only flagged misuse of POCSO in consensual adolescent relationships and urged the Union to consider corrective measures; the age of consent remains 18 (also Section 63 of the BNS) and only Parliament can change it.

questions.q:
Statement-I: On 29 January 2026 the Supreme Court stayed the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, calling them prima facie vague and capable of misuse.
Statement-II: As a result of the stay, the UGC Regulations, 2012 stand repealed and no equity framework applies to higher education institutions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi stayed the 2026 Regulations, which had replaced the 2012 framework and required every institution to set up an Equal Opportunity Centre and an Equity Committee. Using Article 142, the Court directed that the 2012 Regulations continue until further orders, so Statement-II is incorrect.

questions.q:
In January 2026 the Governors' addresses to the State Legislatures in Tamil Nadu and Kerala drew controversy. Consider the following statements:
1. The Tamil Nadu Governor omitted paragraphs of the address, while the Kerala Governor walked out of the Assembly.
2. Article 176 requires the Governor to address the Legislature at the commencement of the first session each year.
3. Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker (2016), cited in the debate, was decided by a five-judge Constitution Bench.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 swaps the facts: it was the Tamil Nadu Governor who walked out and the Kerala Governor who omitted paragraphs. Article 176 provides for the special address at the first session of each year (and after each general election), and Nabam Rebia (2016) was a five-judge Bench ruling on the Governor's discretion.

questions.q: The Mizoram Governor extended Governor's Rule in the Chakma Autonomous District Council by six months in January 2026. Which one of the following is correct about autonomous district councils under the Sixth Schedule?
o: Each council has up to 40 members, all elected on adult franchise, for a six-year term
Each council has up to 30 members, all nominated by the Governor on the advice of the State Council of Ministers
Every council has 46 members, like the Bodoland Territorial Council, of whom six are nominated by the President
Each council has up to 30 members, of whom up to four are nominated by the Governor and the rest elected, for a five-year term
questions.e: Sixth Schedule councils (Chakma ADC was constituted in 1972) have up to 30 members with up to four nominated by the Governor, which gives the usual 26 elected members; the term is five years. Bodoland Territorial Council, with 46 members, is the exception rather than the rule, and nomination is by the Governor, not the President.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth (CSPOC) held in January 2026:
1. It was inaugurated in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan by the President of India.
2. Presiding officers from 42 Commonwealth countries and four semi-autonomous parliaments attended.
3. CSPOC was created in 1969 on the initiative of a Canadian Speaker, and Canada provides its secretariat.
4. It was the first time India hosted the CSPOC.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The conference was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in the chair, so 1 is wrong. India had hosted CSPOC earlier in 1971, 1986 and 2010, so 4 is wrong; 2 and 3 are correct (CSPOC dates to 1969, founded on Lucien Lamoureux's initiative).

questions.q:
The President recently appointed Shri Praveen Vashista as a Vigilance Commissioner in the Central Vigilance Commission. With reference to the CVC and the Lokpal, consider the following statements:
1. The CVC was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
2. The Selection Committee for the Lokpal comprises the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, the CJI or his nominee and the Union Home Minister.
3. The CVC acquired statutory status through the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
4. Vigilance Commissioners are appointed on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the CJI and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 is correct. The Lokpal's Selection Committee has an eminent jurist, not the Home Minister; the CVC became statutory through the CVC Act, 2003; and the appointment committee for the CVC and Vigilance Commissioners is the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Leader of Opposition (the CJI is not on it).

questions.q:
Match List-I (State) with List-II (year of attaining statehood):
List-I: A. Himachal Pradesh  B. Tripura  C. Arunachal Pradesh  D. Sikkim
List-II: 1. 1971  2. 1972  3. 1975  4. 1987
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Himachal Pradesh became the 18th State on 25 January 1971 (State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970). Tripura, with Manipur and Meghalaya, became a State on 21 January 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971; Sikkim joined in 1975 (36th Amendment) and Arunachal Pradesh gained statehood in 1987 (55th Amendment).

questions.q:
Himachal Pradesh marked its 56th Statehood Day on 25 January 2026. Arrange the following statuses it held in chronological order:
1. Union Territory
2. Part C State
3. Full-fledged State
4. Chief Commissioner's Province
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Himachal began as a Chief Commissioner's Province on 15 April 1948, became a Part C State in 1950, and was made a Union Territory on 1 November 1956 after the States Reorganisation Act. It finally became the 18th State on 25 January 1971.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. National Voters' Day, observed on 25 January, marks the anniversary of the first general election of 1951-52.
2. At the India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management 2026, ECINET was launched to integrate over 40 apps of the Election Commission of India into one platform.
3. The conference was hosted by the Election Commission of India at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: National Voters' Day (since 2011) marks the foundation day of the ECI on 25 January 1950, not the first election, so 1 is wrong. IICDEM 2026 was held at Bharat Mandapam, not Vigyan Bhawan, where ECINET was launched and the Delhi Declaration 2026 adopted.

questions.q: The Ministry of Rural Development launched 'Land Stack' in January 2026. Which one of the following best describes it?
o: A blockchain-based property tax portal for urban local bodies run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
A satellite-based crop insurance platform linking farm parcels to Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana claims
A GIS-based integrated digital platform for land records under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme, piloted in Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu
A national registry of village common lands maintained by the Survey of India
questions.e: Land Stack integrates spatial and textual land data in one platform and is inspired by models in Singapore, the UK and Finland. It was launched along with a Glossary of Revenue Terms that harmonises land-revenue vocabulary across languages and scripts. It is a rural land-records reform, not an urban tax or insurance tool.

questions.q:
The Ministry of Home Affairs notified the 16th Census in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The house-listing phase, from 1 April to 30 September 2026, gives each State/UT a 90-day window.
2. The population enumeration phase has a reference date of 1 March 2027.
3. For the snow-bound areas of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the reference date is 1 October 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Each State/UT gets a 30-day window for house-listing, preceded by a 15-day self-enumeration option, so 1 is wrong. The Census under the Census Act, 1948 is India's first digital census and the first nationwide caste enumeration since 1931.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the blocking of illegal betting websites in January 2026, after which the total blocked reached 7,800:
1. Betting and gambling is a subject in the Union List.
2. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 bars banks and financial institutions from processing payments for real-money gaming.
3. Platforms can be blocked under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Betting and gambling fall under Entry 34 of the State List, which is why the Union relies on the IT Act, 2000 blocking power and on payment-channel curbs under the 2025 Act, rather than a direct gambling law. So 1 is wrong while 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about District Mineral Foundations (DMFs), in the news after an Allahabad High Court ruling in January 2026:
1. The High Court held that creating DMFs is beneficial legislation to be interpreted liberally in favour of persons adversely affected by mining.
2. DMFs are statutory non-profit trusts under Section 9B of the MMDR Act, 1957.
3. Lessees contribute 10% of royalty for leases granted before 12 January 2015 and 30% for later leases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The contribution rates are the other way round: 30% of royalty for leases before 12 January 2015 and 10% for later ones. Section 9B was inserted in 2015, and DMF money is spent under the Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana with at least 60% for high-priority areas.

questions.q: In a petition filed by Dr Jaya Thakur, the Supreme Court in January 2026 dealt with menstrual health in schools. Which one of the following correctly states its position?
o: It declared menstrual leave for schoolgirls a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g)

It treated menstrual health and hygiene management in schools as part of the right to life and dignity under Article 21, and directed functional gender-segregated toilets and free sanitary napkins in every school
It held menstrual hygiene to be only a Directive Principle under Article 47, not enforceable against the State
It directed Parliament to enact a Menstrual Hygiene Act within six months
questions.e: The Court read menstrual hygiene into Article 21, so the duty is enforceable, and directed States and UTs to provide vending machines for free sanitary napkins and set up MHM corners. Article 47 (public health) is a Directive Principle, but the Court's reasoning rests on the Fundamental Right to life with dignity.

questions.q: The Lokpal of India observed its Foundation Day on 16 January 2026. This date commemorates
o: The first Chairperson of the Lokpal taking oath of office
The introduction of the first Lokpal Bill in Lok Sabha in 1968
Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 coming into force on 16 January 2014
The recommendation of the Santhanam Committee to set up an anti-corruption body
questions.e: The Foundation Day marks Section 3 coming into force in 2014, not the later appointment of the first Chairperson. The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, at least 50% of them judicial members. Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.

questions.q: The National Dam Safety Authority issued a show-cause notice to the Narmada Valley Development Authority over safety concerns at Bargi Dam. Which one of the following is correct?
o: NDSA is a statutory body under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, and Bargi Dam is on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh
NDSA is a constitutional body under Article 262, and Bargi Dam is on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh
NDSA is a statutory body under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, and Bargi Dam is on the Chambal in Rajasthan
NDSA is an executive body under the Ministry of Environment, and Bargi Dam is on the Tapi in Gujarat
questions.e: NDSA is created by the Dam Safety Act, 2021 and is headquartered in New Delhi; it is not constitutional (Article 262 deals with inter-State river disputes) and works under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Bargi, built between 1974 and 1990 as a multipurpose dam, is on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Budget Session of Parliament 2026:
1. It began on 28 January 2026.
2. The Finance Bill, 2026 and two Appropriation Bills were among nine Government Bills passed.
3. The session concluded in the second week of March 2026, before the Houses took up non-financial legislation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The session ran from 28 January to 18 April 2026, so it did not end in March, and non-financial bills such as the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 and the Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026 were also passed within it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026:
1. They apply only to central universities.
2. Every higher education institution must set up an Equal Opportunity Centre and an Equity Committee.
3. The Equity Committee must meet within 24 hours of a complaint and report within 15 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Regulations cover every higher education institution, not just central universities, and replaced the 2012 framework with new bodies, Equity Squads, a 24x7 helpline and penalties up to loss of UGC recognition. The head of the institution has to act within 7 days. (The Supreme Court stayed them on 29 January 2026.)

questions.q: The Supreme Court asked the Union government to respond to a petition seeking constitution of the Arbitration Council of India. Which one of the following is correct about the Council?
o: It is a constitutional body under Article 323B, created in 2019 and functioning since
It was constituted in 2019 on the recommendation of the Law Commission and has been grading arbitral institutions since
It is provided in the Arbitration Act, 1940 and was revived by an Ordinance in 2015
It is a statutory body under Part IA of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, provided by the 2019 Amendment, but has still not been constituted
questions.e: Sections 43A to 43M were inserted by the 2019 Amendment on the basis of the Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee (2017), yet nearly six years later the Council has not been set up. Article 323B concerns tribunals for specified matters, not arbitration.

questions.q: The Supreme Court directed all States to frame a policy on police media briefings, arising out of PUCL petitions. The 2014 judgment in which case laid down 16 guidelines on police encounters?
o: Basu v. State of West Bengal (D.K. Basu)
Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
questions.e: PUCL v. State of Maharashtra (2014) set out 16 guidelines for investigating police encounter deaths. The Basu case deals with arrest and custody safeguards, Lalita Kumari with mandatory FIR registration for cognizable offences, and Prakash Singh with police reforms.

questions.q:
Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura celebrated their statehood anniversary on 21 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. They became full States on 21 January 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
2. The same Act made the North-East Frontier Agency the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh.
3. Arunachal Pradesh attained statehood in 1987 through the 55th Constitutional Amendment.
4. Tribal areas of Tripura are administered under the Fifth Schedule.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Tripura's tribal areas come under the Sixth Schedule (as Meghalaya's do), not the Fifth, which covers Scheduled Areas in other States; Manipur's hill areas have separate safeguards under Article 371C.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India has no single national list of notifiable diseases, and it is for States and Union Territories to notify diseases, as Delhi announced it would do for human rabies under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
Statement-II: Public health and sanitation is a subject in the State List.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because public health and sanitation is Entry 6 of the State List, each State/UT decides its own list of notifiable diseases (snakebite was added by some in 2024). The Centre's role is mainly surveillance through the IDSP run by the NCDC, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q: Who was elected national president of the Bharatiya Janata Party on 20 January 2026, becoming the party's youngest national president?
questions.e: Nitin Nabin, earlier the BJP's working president and a Bihar minister representing Bankipur, was elected during the party's Sangathan Parv, with the result announced by national returning officer Dr K. Laxman. J.P. Nadda was his predecessor.
